tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Where this account stands: credit, when free credit ends, prompts waiting to be tested, tests so far, and what to do next. Free.

tools.name: load_prompts
tools.description: Load prompts and their examples into the account for the person to review and run. Spends nothing. Returns a link to show them.

tools.name: run_loaded_prompt
tools.description: Test a prompt from load_prompts, using its cases and checks and drafting any that are missing. Spends credit, never more than max_spend_usd by estimate. Call get_test for the results.

tools.name: test_prompt
tools.description: Start a test of one prompt across several models. Spends credit, never more than max_spend_usd by estimate. Returns at once with a test_id: call get_test for the results. Cases and checks are drafted if left out.

tools.name: get_test
tools.description: A test's status and, when done, what it found: the best model, each model's pass rate and cost, and sample failures.

tools.name: improve_prompt
tools.description: Rewrite a finished test's prompt from its failures and ratings, then test the new version on the same cases, checks and models. Spends credit.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: Models a test can use, with prices, and the credit left on this account.

tools.name: rating_link
tools.description: A link that lets anyone rate a test's answers on their phone, with no account and the models hidden. Send it to whoever knows what good looks like. Anyone with the link can read those answers and inputs, so ask before sharing.

tools.name: train_judge
tools.description: Train a judge on a test's ratings. It's tested on answers it hasn't seen, and only kept if it beats always giving the commoner verdict. Spends a little credit.

tools.name: list_judges
tools.description: This account's trained judges, and how often each agreed with its rater.

tools.name: score_answers
tools.description: Score up to 50 answers with a trained judge: how likely the person it learned from is to call each one good, from 0 to 1. Spends a little credit.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: load_prompts · Public sink: rating_link · Destructive: load_prompts, run_loaded_prompt.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: load_prompts · Public sink: rating_link · Destructive: load_prompts, run_loaded_prompt

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
